title: Pages Router vs App Router
definition: The architectural differences between the legacy Next.js routing system (`pages/`) and the modern routing system (`app/`).
simpleExplanation: Pages router: Fetched data at the page level using weird Next.js specific functions like `getServerSideProps`. App router: Uses standard async/await directly inside React components, and leverages React Server Components.
realWorldExample: Migrating an old Next.js 12 blog to Next.js 14, changing `export async function getStaticProps` into standard `const data = await fetch()` inside the component.

basic: Which router is the recommended, modern way to build Next.js applications?
intermediate: Can you use the `pages` and `app` router in the same project?

answers.question: Use both simultaneously?
answers.answer: Yes! Next.js supports incremental adoption. You can have both directories running at the same time, allowing you to migrate an enterprise app one page at a time.
